title: "Find packages used by my shiny apps"
author: "CE"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(flextable)
```

This Rmarkdown file checks all the R files and finds where they call packages whether by loading the package or using a "package::function()" call and it gets round a few challenges that could hide packages.  Here is the list of the packages in alphabetic order.

```{r}
list.files(pattern = "*.R$", recursive = TRUE) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  rename(file = value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(lines = list(readLines(str_c("./", file), warn = FALSE))) %>%
  unnest_longer(lines) %>%
  ### we don't need the files
  select(-file) %>%
  distinct() -> tmpTib

tmpTib %>% 
  filter(str_detect(lines, fixed("library("))) %>%
  ### get rid of "suppressMessages(" as these make parsing harder
  mutate(lines = str_remove(lines,  fixed("suppressMessages("))) %>%
  ### ditto "suppressWarnings(" as these make parsing harder
  mutate(lines = str_remove(lines,  fixed("suppressWarnings("))) %>%
  mutate(library = str_replace(lines, "^(.*?)library\\((.*?)\\)(.*)$", "\\2")) %>% 
  select(library) %>%
  distinct() -> tmpTibLibrary

tmpTib %>%
  ### don't reanalyse the filter lines
  filter_out(str_detect(lines, fixed("library("))) %>%
  filter(str_detect(lines, fixed("::"))) %>%
  ### get rid of "suppressMessages(" as these make parsing harder
  mutate(lines = str_remove(lines,  fixed("suppressMessages("))) %>%
  ### ditto "suppressWarnings(" as these make parsing harder
  mutate(lines = str_remove(lines,  fixed("suppressWarnings("))) %>%
  ### now parse simple lines without a RtL assigment
  mutate(library = str_replace(lines, "^(.*?)\\:\\:(.*)$", "\\1"),
         library = str_replace(library, "^(.*?)[[:space:]]{1,1}([[:alnum:]]+)", "\\2"),
         ### now do that again to catch the lines with RtL assigment (and so early spaces)
         library = str_replace(library, "^(.*?)[[:space:]]{1,1}([[:alnum:]]+)", "\\2"),
         ### now handle "package::" within allocations to list
         library = str_remove(library, fixed("list("))) %>%
  select(-lines) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  bind_rows(tmpTibLibrary) %>%
  distinct() -> tibLibraries

tibLibraries %>%
  arrange(library) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  autofit()
```

Now it checks whether they are installed on your system and if some are missing it shows you a list of those missings ones next, otherwise you should see "There are no packages unavailable on your system".

```{r checkInstalled}
installed.packages()[, 1] %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  rename(installedLibrary = value) -> tibInstalled

tibLibraries %>%
  filter(!library %in% tibInstalled$installedLibrary) -> tibMissing

if(nrow(tibMissing) > 0) {
  tibMissing %>%
    rename(missingPackage = library) %>%
    select(missingPackage) %>%
    pull() -> vecMissingPackages
  
  save(vecMissingPackages, file = "vecMissingPackages.Rda")
  
  write_csv(tibMissing, file = "missingPackages.csv")
  
  tmpTxt <- "**You have the following missing packages**"
} else {
  tmpTxt <- "**There are no packages unavailable in your system**"
  
}
```

`r tmpTxt`

```{r missingPackages2}
if (nrow(tibMissing) > 0) {
  tibMissing %>%
    flextable() %>%
    autofit()
}
```

So if you have successfully run the code and it has found you are missing some packages the code will also have created a vector of those package names and saved that into a file "vecMissingPackages.Rda" which you can load from within an R session with:  
`load(file = "vecMissingPackages.Rda")`.  

I've also stored it as a csv file "missingPackages.csv" which should read in with:  
`read.csv(file = "missingPackages.csv") -> vecMissingPackages`.

Once you have that vector in an R session you should also be able to install the missing packages with 
`install.packages(vecMissingPackages, ask = TRUE, checkBuilt = TRUE)`

You may find that some of the missing packages aren't on CRAN, for example my own CECPfuns package.  The instructions to install that, and more about it are at [https://cecpfuns.psyctc.org](https://cecpfuns.psyctc.org).  Others you may have to do a bit of internet searching to discover where they live and how to install them.  If you have problems despite searching, do please [contact me](https://www.psyctc.org/psyctc/contact-me/).
